content: Akari's CURRENT resolved graph contradicts two CONTEXT SPIKE-02 landmine rows. src/AkariTool.App/obj/project.assets.json resolves Microsoft.Windows.CsWinRT 2.1.1, not 2.0.4: the 2.0.4 pin lives in vendor/WinGet.Interop and is lower so NuGet takes the max, and 2.1.1 arrives from the Material.Icons.WinUI3 3.0.2 nuspec. It also resolves Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools 10.0.26100.4654, NOT absent, which is exactly Winhance's pinned version, even though no Akari csproj names it. Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.WinUI 2.3.0 is already present transitively via the metapackage, which is the supported pattern; the MSB4011 hazard is only adding it as a DIRECT reference alongside the metapackage. CsWinRT is NOT a nuspec dependency of any WCT 8.2 package, so it must be added explicitly; Microsoft.Windows.CsWinRT 2.2.0 and stable 2.3.1 (published 2026-07-22) both exist, owner Microsoft, zero package deps. Verified hard error text in Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.Base.targets lines 19-20: target WindowsAppSDKSelfContainedAudit BeforeTargets Build, condition WindowsAppSDKSelfContained true AND OutputType Library, Error 'WindowsAppSDKSelfContained should not be applied to a class library.' Therefore tools/run-tests.ps1 must never pass /p:WindowsAppSDKSelfContained=true or /p:SelfContained=true globally, or all five library projects (Core, Infrastructure, WinGet.Interop, WinUI.Framework, App.Tests) hard-fail. Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Markup.Compiler.BeforeCommon.targets line 22 also forces WindowsAppSDKSelfContained=false in the markup-compile step, and Microsoft.WinUI.NET.Markup.Compiler.targets line 53 has a Library-specific condition, so library output is anticipated rather than an error case.
